trace: 4 Background --> 4.1 Introduction --> Figure 4.1-1 Common Application Life Cycle Management for ASD

text:
* Step 1, DELIVER: a solution provider \(vendor\) delivers an application package \(app package\) which may include a variety of artifacts. These artifacts may include application descriptors, model descriptors, informational artifacts, cloud native artifacts, metadata, and dictionaries.
  * Step 2, ONBOARDING: Onboarding involves the ingestion, verification, and unpacking of the package and storage into a catalog. The SMO performs these onboarding activities and may usea cloud-native onboarding tools for that purpose. During this process, an AI/ML model can be trained. 
    * o Security Package Validation During onboarding, the security validation of the package or package artifact\(s\) is performed. See the OAM Architecture document \[1\] clause 4.1.3, and clause 4.1.4.
  * Step 3, CERTIFICATION PROCESS: After onboarding, the package undergoes a certification process from the catalog in the SMO. Afterwards, it is published to an artifact repository \(aka the run-time library\). Certification of the package may include the following: security validation of artifacts, metadata verification, artifact verification against indicated metadata locations. See the OAM Architecture document \[1\]. 
    * o Note: The package cannot be certified until training is finished. If the AI/ML training cannot complete, the package is not certified.
    * o Note: The package cannot be certified until security validation of the package is completed.
    * o Note: For some operators, the package may go through part of the certification process before onboarding \(Step 1 and Step 2\).
  * Step 4, DEPLOY: In deployment, The deployment tool is given a reference to the image repository entry from which the image can be pulled. Inventory is updated.

text: 4.2.2 App Package Security
trace: 4 Background --> 4.2.2 App Package Security

text: An important aspect of managing application packages of CNFs, VNFs, rApps, and xApps as it relates to O-RAN Cloudification & Orchestration are the security aspects.
trace: 4 Background --> 4.2.2 App Package Security

text: The WG11 Security Requirements specification \[12\] covers security requirements and controls related to package security. These requirements follow ETSI GS NFV-SEC 021 \[11\], ETSI GS NFV-IFA011 \[3\] \(stage 2\) and ETSI GS NFV-SOL 004 \[2\] Clause 5.1 \(stage 3\) which describes two options for package security:
trace: 4 Background --> 4.2.2 App Package Security

text: Option 1 Per Artifact: The VNF package shall contain a Digest \(a.k.a. hash\) for each of the components of the VNF package. The table of hashes is included in the manifest file, which is signed with the VNF provider private key. In addition, the VNF provider shall include a signing certificate that includes the VNF provider public key, following a pre-defined naming convention and located either at the root of the archive or in a predefined location \(e.g., directory\). The certificate may also be included in the signature container if the signature format allows that. For example, the CMS format allows to include the certificate in the same container as the signature.
trace: 4 Background --> 4.2.2 App Package Security

text: All package artifacts shall be individually signed by the VNF provider as per ETSI GS NFV-SOL 004 \[2\] Clause 5.4 \(stage 3\) and the WG11 Security Requirements specification \[12\].
trace: 4 Background --> 4.2.2 App Package Security

text: Option 2 Per CSAR Package: The complete CSAR file shall be digitally signed with the VNF provider private key. The VNF provider delivers one zip file consisting of the CSAR file, a signature file and a certificate file that includes the VNF provider public key. Only one signature of the CSAR file shall be present. The certificate may also be included in the signature container if the signature format allows that. The manifest shall be signed in both option 1 and option 2. Only one signature of the manifest shall be present.

description:
The diagram illustrates the deployment flow use case in a Service Management & Orchestration (SMO) framework. The process begins with an orchestration trigger from a Cloud Operator initiating a deployment. Initially, deployment requirements parameters flow from the Cloud Operator to an Orchestration block. This trigger leads to a complex "Homing Operation" sequence:

1. "Deployment Initiated" from Cloud Operator to Orchestration.
2. [Optional] "Collect Input & Parameterizations" from Deployment Requirements to Orchestration.
3. "Homing Operation (Cluster ID not provided)" from Orchestration to Homing Operation.
    - Determining a K8s cluster matching constraints and resource requirements. Two optional actions are depicted within "Homing Operation (Cluster ID not provided)" block.
4. "Homing Operation (Cluster ID already provided)" from Orchestration to Homing Operation.
    - Checking inventory for resources and constraints from Deployment Description.
5. "Homing Operation Cluster ID cannot be fulfilled", which can have three outcomes:
    - [Homing Operation (Cluster ID already provided)].
    - "No Free Resources or constraints not fulfilled" from Homing Operation to Cloud Operator.
6. "[Optional] Homing Operation Cluster has special configuration needed" from Homing Operation to FOCOM/IMS to configure the cluster.

Once a specific cluster is determined and configured, the flow moves to the deployment stage. The sequence is as follows:
7. "Cluster ID and parameterized cloud artifacts" from Homing Operation to Orchestration, followed by Deployment Tools.
8. "Deployment" from Orchestration to Deployment Tools.
9. "A Cloud Native Descriptor (CN Descriptor) file" from the deployment to an Orchestration component.
10. "DDeployment complete" from Deployment to Cloud Operator.

1. "Request NF Deployment instantiation" from Cloud Operator to SMO
2. "Get VNFD of the NF Deployment from Application Package" from SMO to NFO

4. "NFO coordination with FOCOM to check O-Cloud availability" from SMO to FOCOM
55. "Check O-Cloud inventory, capacity and resources availability of of O-Cloud" from FOCOM to SMO
6. "NF Deployment homing processing and decision" from SMO to NFO
7. "[Successful homing]" or "[Unsuccessful NF Deployment instantiation]" from SMO to Cloud Operator
 8. "Request NF Deployment instantiation" from Cloud Operator to SMO
 9. "Request necessary Application Package content" from Cloud Operator to O-Cloud DMS
10. "Inform about successful instantiation" from O-Cloud DMS to Cloud Operator
11. "Update necessary runtime and inventory information" from Cloud Operator to Cloud Operator
12. "Inform about unsuccessful instantiation" from Cloud Operator to O-Cloud DMS
13. "Release granted/reserved resources and update of necessary inventory information" from Cloud Operator to Cloud Operator
14. "Inform result of NF Deployment instantiation" from Cloud Operator to Cloud Operator

* The "Attribute" column provides the attribute name.
